newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GLOBUS SEES SALES, PROFIT INCREASE IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: GLOBUS SEES SALES, PROFIT INCREASE IN 1997.

text.p: Hungarian canned food producer Globus plans to boost its net sales and profit this year as it expects a rise in household consumption in Hungary, Globus said on Friday.

"We plan total net sales of 6.5 billion forints... and a pre-tax profit of 195 million forints for 1996," Globus chief executive officer Miklos Olah told Reuters following the annual meeting of the company's shareholders.

Globus posted a pre-tax profit of 169.35 million forints in 1996 on net sales of 5.38 billion forints, compared with a pre-tax profit of 260.7 million forints in 1995 on net sales revenues of 5,65 billion forints.
Olah said the company's net sales fell in 1996 due to the recession which hit Hungary's consumer goods market, especially processed food products, last year.
However, the decline of real wages is expected to reverse this year and Globus plans to take advantage of that, he said.
"We trust the government's forecast that consumption and demand will increase this year," Olah said.
Within the 1997 net sales, some 420 to 430 million forints will be generated from goods, which Globus buys for resale, he added.

Olah confirmed the information of the Hungarian MTI news agency that Globus would pay 12 percent dividend in a total amount of 119.6 million forints on the 1996 earnings instead of the originally planned eight percent.
The board of directors changed its original plan as the company did not need the profits to finance its activities, while it wanted to please shareholders, Olah said.
On the 1995 earnings Globus paid eight percent dividend.
Olah said the company did not give up its ambitions for an international share or bond offering, to finance the planned expansion of its production capacities in Hungary, Germany and the Ukraine.
"Our acquisition plans have not come to the stage yet that we could have proposed a share issue to the shareholders meeting," he said.

He added that according to the company's estimate, Globus would need to raise one to three billion forints through the share or bond issue, but the amount depended on the outcome of the acquisition talks.
Globus will choose to issue bonds if the amount needed is relatively small, Olah said.
Globus closed at 2,050 forints on the Budapest Stock Exchange, up 50 forints.
